title: The Farmer Who Stopped Elephants With Bees 🐘🐝
yt_title: The Farmer Who Stopped Elephants With Bees 🐘🐝
yt_description:
The whole village laughed when Amina hung empty boxes around her corn… until the elephants came. 🐘🐝
Elephants are afraid of honey bees. In a nine-year study next to Tsavo East National Park in Kenya, beehive fences kept away about 76% of approaching elephants (up to 86% in peak crop season), and the hives produced honey for the farmers. (Amina is a fictional character; the beehive fences are real science.)

Sources: King et al. (2024), Conservation Science and Practice; University of Oxford / Save the Elephants press release (Oct 2024); King, Douglas-Hamilton & Vollrath, beehive fence field trials, northern Kenya.

script: This farmer hangs empty wooden boxes on a wire around her corn. And the whole village thinks she has lost her mind. Every night, elephants walk out of the bush. One hungry herd can wipe out a whole field before sunrise. Her neighbor bangs pots, lights fires, and builds a fence of thorns. Nothing works. But Amina hangs wooden boxes on a long wire, every few steps, all the way around her field. The village laughs. Boxes? Against elephants? They weigh six tons! Then Amina does something even stranger. She moves a swarm of bees into every box. The village laughs even louder. Bees? Against elephants? Amina just smiles. And waits. That night, a giant trunk bumps the wire. The boxes swing. And the bees wake up, buzzing like a storm. The elephants turn around and hurry away. Ears flapping, trunks up, straight back into the bush. By harvest, her corn stands tall, and she has jars of honey to sell. Her neighbor's field is flattened. That night, the neighbor knocks on her door. Amina... can I borrow some bees? Elephants really are afraid of bees. In a nine year study in Kenya, beehive fences kept away about three out of four elephants. And they made honey too.
